priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock, held after the red team but rebuilt on a different foundation. The draft held WATCH because the forward ask looked cheap and was capped by capture and a partly-unwound multiple. The red team finds the forward ask is not cheap, it is unmeasured: quality.reverse_dcf.base_fcf of $232.195M is exactly FY2025 free cash flow and 2.90x the FY2022-2025 average of $80.020M, so the 7.0% implied five-year FCF CAGR is a floor on the price's demand rather than a measurement of it (EV is 19.11x FY2025 FCF and 55.45x the four-year average). The claimed gap fails its own method test as well: 8.5% against 7.0% is 1.50pp, inside the file's 1.95pp horizon_spread, and method section 7 says a gap inside the band is not a gap, though here a longer horizon widens rather than closes it. Capture is now measured instead of inherited and it confirms the 40 score from the filings: between the FY2018-2021 and FY2022-2025 windows average revenue rose 63.8% while average free cash flow rose 24.6% and FCF margin fell from 3.08% to 2.34%, with FCF negative in FY2023. The 5.5% steady-state operating margin is above all eight fiscal years on disk (range 1.608% to 4.746%, mean 3.522%), and the only mechanism this dive quotes for the current level is management's own non-recurring 'favorable job close outs'. Crowdedness is worse than unresolved: the price series refutes 'undiscovered' directly (a 19.85% single-session gap on 2026-04-30, 2.883x off the 2025-09-15 low, then -41.25%), and the dive relied on the analyst count of 5 as evidence for its thesis while ruling the same number unusable against it. What survives intact and independently confirmed: growth is real (LTM revenue to 2026-06-30 reconstructs to exactly $4,006.051M from the market file's own quarterly and annual series, up 16.06% on the prior LTM, Q2 up 20.15% YoY), the balance sheet is net cash, and the mechanical battery is clean (Piotroski 8, Beneish -2.206, Altman 5.97). One correction runs the bull's way: at 294.42 the stock is already below the 2026-04-08 close of 300.43, so the entire leg that produced the peak has essentially round-tripped, and the draft's 'only 41% unwound' framing measured against the peak was the wrong denominator for whether the unwind is done. Verdict holds at WATCH, not because the odds look balanced but because the central number is unmeasurable from what is on disk. That is not TOO_LATE, which would need the decomposition to show the outcome already priced and would open a directional shadow row against SPY after a 41% drawdown that this evidence does not support, and it is not INVESTABLE, which would need an entry basis resting on a forward ask the red team just found unanchored.
bull: The forward bar the price sets is low IF the base year is representative: the reverse DCF implies a 7.0% five-year free-cash-flow CAGR (5.05% at ten years) off a base FCF of $232.195M, against a 6.7312% three-year revenue CAGR already achieved. The growth underneath it is real and independently confirmed: LTM revenue to 2026-06-30 reconstructs to exactly $4,006.051M from the market file's own quarterly and annual series, matching the 8-K figure to the dollar, up 16.06% on the prior LTM of $3,451.783M, with Q2 2026 alone up 20.15% YoY. RED TEAM: the conditional is load-bearing and was not in the draft. FY2025 free cash flow of $232.195M is 2.90x the FY2022-2025 average of $80.020M, so the bar is low only if that year repeats.

Balance sheet imposes no constraint on riding the buildout: net debt to EBITDA of -0.5705x (net cash, $137.872M cash against $4.722M total debt at 2026-06-30), Piotroski 8 of 9 (STRONG, 9 of 9 inputs present), Altman Z 5.97 (SAFE), and a clean Beneish M-score of -2.206 against a -1.78 review threshold (12 of 12 inputs present). Nothing in the mechanical earnings-quality battery is broken, and the red team re-ran all four against the same market file and reproduced every value.

Sits on the single highest-criticality bottleneck in the whole twelve-link chain, grid-interconnect, bottleneck criticality HIGH and named as the chain's slowest step, with double-sided exposure: the T&D segment builds the interconnection itself and the C&I segment names data centers among the facility types it wires, plus two acquisitions (Valley Electric and Comet Electric, closed 2026-07-01) that management says enhance the C&I side specifically. RED TEAM: the bottleneck-criticality and money-corner half of this bullet is inherited from the chain and heat blocks, which the red team is forbidden to read, so it is recorded as unverified from the dive-plus-market-file boundary rather than confirmed.
bear: Capture fails the eight-year conversion test, computed here rather than inherited. Between the FY2018-2021 and FY2022-2025 windows, average revenue rose 63.8% ($2,087.0M to $3,418.2M) while average free cash flow rose only 24.6% ($64.209M to $80.020M), and the free-cash-flow margin FELL from 3.08% to 2.34%. Over the same eight years revenue compounded 13.25% a year and free cash flow was negative in one of them (FY2023, -$13.720M) and $11.177M in another (FY2024). Volume at this link demonstrably has not reached cash at anything like the rate of revenue growth across a full cycle, which is what a bid-competed contractor margin (4.562% GAAP operating margin in FY2025) looks like from the cash-flow statement rather than from a chain score.

The 5.5% steady-state operating margin in the gap table sits above EVERY full fiscal year in the eight-year record, not merely above its mean. Computed from the market file: FY2018 3.286%, FY2019 2.761%, FY2020 3.851%, FY2021 4.746%, FY2022 3.819%, FY2023 3.543%, FY2024 1.608%, FY2025 4.562%; n=8, range 1.608% to 4.746%, mean 3.522%. The swing is estimate revision, not operating leverage: FY2023 to FY2024 operating income fell 58.1% on revenue down 7.7%, then FY2024 to FY2025 it rose 208.6% on revenue up 8.8%. Management's own stated driver for the favorable phase is 'significant changes in our estimated gross profit on certain projects, related to better-than-anticipated productivity, favorable job close outs', and a close-out is non-recurring by construction.

The reverse DCF's base year is a 2.90x outlier, so the 'cheap forward bar' is unmeasured rather than measured. quality.reverse_dcf.base_fcf is $232.195M, which is exactly FY2025 free cash flow and 2.90x the FY2022-2025 average of $80.020M. On FY2025 FCF the enterprise value of $4,437.083M is 19.11x; on the four-year average it is 55.45x. The same year carries the dive's own accrual flag (-13.29% of average assets, OCF at 2.7578x net income, called probable working-capital timing), so the reverse DCF is anchored on the year the dive itself says overstates durable cash generation, and an inflated base UNDERSTATES the implied growth bar. Separately the multiple point stands: price rose 107.24% from 2023-08-31 to 2026-08-28 while revenue per share rose 7.90% ($218.40 to $235.65), P/S 0.6505x to 1.2494x.

crowdedness.basis: The two axes disagree and this dive does not resolve the conflict by picking the flattering one. Axis A reads DARK at 73.5 but its own gate is ADVISORY, so it carries no control-passed status. Axis B reads SATURATED but the number behind the band, 5 analysts, is genuinely thin, and its paired institutional-ownership field is unusable. I therefore rely on the chain-level heat judgment instead of either issuer axis: Ember scored grid-interconnect UNDISCOVERED (impact 70, crowdedness 30, capture 40, as_of 2026-08-28), an analytical call about the corner ('quietest corner of the chain in retail terms... EPC names get episodic attention, utilities almost none as AI plays'), not a measurement of this specific issuer. That is a weaker foundation than a clean issuer-level PCS read would be, and it is stated as such rather than smoothed over.
crowdedness.counter_evidence: The price series argues against a clean 'nobody is looking' story regardless of which PCS axis is right: MYRG rallied from a 2025-09-15 low of 173.81 to a 2026-06-29 high of 501.13, roughly 2.88x in about nine months, then gave back 41.3% to 294.42 by 2026-08-28, with the decline beginning before, not after, the Q2 2026 earnings release that reported record results. Something bid this name up hard and then sold it off hard; that is not the price behavior of a name nobody has found, whatever the PCS axes say. Flagged for the red team's CROWDEDNESS_REALITY attack rather than resolved here.
crowdedness.red_team_finding: CROWDEDNESS_REALITY landed. Two things, both checkable from the dive and the market file alone. (1) Internal contradiction: independence_test.why_the_gap_exists rests on 'only 5 sell-side analysts' as the reason a mispricing can persist, while this block dismisses PCS axis_b, whose band SATURATED is built on that same analyst_count of 5, as not usable. The dive cannot treat the analyst count as decisive evidence for its thesis and as unusable evidence against it. Note also that axis_b carries no gate caveat at all in data/market/MYRG.json; the ADVISORY gate and the unreadable-fixture reason attach to the pcs block's gate object, and it is axis_a's DARK 73.5 that has no control-passed status behind it. The dive dismissed the cleaner axis and deferred to an inherited chain-level judgment, which is the flattering direction reached by a longer route. (2) The price series refutes 'undiscovered' outright: +19.85% in a single session on 2026-04-30 (337.76 to 404.81), 2.883x from the 2025-09-15 low of 173.81 to the 2026-06-29 high of 501.13, then -41.25% back to 294.42. A security that gaps 20% in a day and halves in two months is being actively repriced by someone, whatever either axis reports. UNRESOLVED was the honest label for the measurement and the evasive one for the conclusion: the measurement genuinely cannot be settled from disk, but the conclusion that this issuer is not crowded is contradicted by evidence already inside the dive.

rows.structural_reason: H1 2026 consolidated operating margin (6.37%) already exceeds every full fiscal year in the 2018-2025 record (prior high 4.75% in FY2021), and it shows up in both segments (T&D 9.6%, C&I 8.3% operating margin in H1 2026 per the 8-K segment table), not one segment's favorable close-outs alone, which is at least consistent with a mix shift toward higher-value work rather than a single-project fluke.
rows.leading_indicator: Quarterly consolidated operating margin sustaining at or above 6% through Q4 2026, rather than reverting toward the FY2018-2024 average of roughly 3.5% once the currently favorable job close-outs (management's own stated driver) roll off. This is watch_triggers[1] on this file.
rows.why: Margin history is volatile and this is a genuinely aggressive assumption relative to it, which is why the structural reason and leading indicator above are both named rather than assumed.
rows.red_team_note: Percentile 85 is understated. 5.5% is above every one of the eight full fiscal years on disk (range 1.608% to 4.746%, mean 3.522%), not merely above the 80th percentile of a base rate. The named structural reason, that H1 2026 already exceeds every full year in the record, restates the observation rather than supplying a mechanism, and the only mechanism actually quoted in this dive is management's own 'favorable job close outs', which is non-recurring. The leading indicator is sound and is kept.

rows.market_implied_note: The solve as filed does not decompose a reinvestment return separately from the headline FCF CAGR. Recorded as a data gap in this row rather than invented.

Base rate (roughly 40-50% of top-quartile ROIC firms stay there after ten years) argues for meaningful decay rather than persistence at 26.7%, so 15% mid-path is a decay case, not an extrapolation of the peak.
rows.leading_indicator: LTM ROIC as disclosed each quarter; a slide back toward the low-to-mid teens over the next two to three quarters would confirm decay, a hold near 25% plus would say the current level is more durable than the base rate implies.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so matters. The solve's 2.5% perpetual growth sits at or below the long-run nominal GDP ceiling this repo's own base rates cite, and is the one input this dive would not change for a bid-competed contractor with no visible moat.

rows.note: The forward-implied bar (7.0% five-year FCF CAGR) is cheap against delivered growth (6.7312% achieved, 20.2% YoY last quarter), which argues for a positive gap. Two things cap it from becoming a clean bullish call: capture at this link is the chain's own trap example (score 40), so volume growth may not convert to equity value at the rate the growth numbers alone would suggest; and about 90% of the stock's two-year price return is already price-to-sales re-rating rather than delivered growth, a re-rating only 41% unwound from its June 2026 peak. Net: modestly positive on the forward numbers, substantially offset by a capture ceiling and a multiple that has not fully round-tripped.
rows.red_team_note: AMENDED by the red team. The draft's direction, modestly bullish on the forward ask, rested on the 7.0% implied CAGR being a measurement of the price's demand. It is not, because its base year is 2.90x the four-year average free cash flow. On the four-year average the same enterprise value is 55.45x free cash flow rather than 19.11x. The honest net direction is therefore not modestly positive and not negative: it is unmeasured, and the two caps the draft named (capture 40, a partly-unwound multiple) apply on top of an unmeasured rather than a cheap forward ask. The capture cap is now measured rather than inherited: average revenue +63.8% against average FCF +24.6% between the two four-year windows.

expectations_gap.red_team_denominator: 5 of 5 required rows populated. Market-implied column, counted honestly over the 4 numeric drivers: 1 SOLVED and category-matched to its own row (terminal, 2.5%, the one row where the dive states no disagreement); 1 SOLVED but category-mismatched (revenue_cagr_5y reads the solved FCF CAGR as a revenue proxy); 1 reasoned rather than solved (operating_margin, the dive says so itself); 1 NULL (reinvestment_return). Every row on which the dive claims a gap therefore has a market-implied column that is a proxy, a reasoning, or absent. That is the finding, not a formatting complaint: the gap table's whole purpose is to make 'not priced in' checkable, and on this file only the row with no disagreement is fully checkable.
expectations_gap.red_team_gap_vs_spread: Method section 7: a gap smaller than horizon_spread must say which of the two it is claiming, and a gap inside the band is not a gap. The revenue row claims 8.5% against 7.0%, a 1.50pp gap, inside the file's 1.95pp horizon_spread. On the default five-year convention the claimed edge is therefore inside the band and is not a gap. The direction matters and cuts the other way from VRT: here the longer horizon LOWERS the implied bar (5y 7.0%, 7y 5.88%, 10y 5.05%), so choosing a ten-year explicit period widens the gap to 3.45pp rather than closing it. The dive's own line, that a 1.95pp spread is 'narrow' so the convention is not load-bearing, tested the wrong quantity: what matters is the gap against the spread, not the spread against some absolute idea of wide. Net: the claimed disagreement survives only on a convention the file does not default to, and the deeper problem is the base, not the horizon.
expectations_gap.red_team_base_fcf: The market-implied column inherits a base. quality.reverse_dcf.base_fcf is $232.195M, exactly FY2025 free cash flow, which is 2.90x the FY2022-2025 average of $80.020M and comes from the year this dive's own earnings_quality section flags at -13.29% accruals to average assets. A base that high makes the solved growth requirement low. This is not solvable in-session (method section 7 forbids re-solving the reverse DCF here) and the file carries no base-FCF sensitivity, so the correct statement is directional and bounded: the 7.0% implied CAGR is a floor on what the price is asking, not a measurement of it, and the same is true of the 5.05% ten-year reading.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market is treating MYR Group's 41.3% drawdown from its 2026-06-29 peak as a correction of a story that ran too far, when the forward-implied growth bar left behind by that drawdown (7.0% five-year FCF CAGR) is now cheap relative to what the company is currently delivering (record backlog up 19.6% YoY, revenue up 20.2% YoY), even though the underlying multiple has not returned to its pre-story 2023 level.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: This looks like a thin-coverage momentum unwind rather than a fundamentals-driven repricing: with only 5 sell-side analysts and no dedicated data-center or grid-capex segment disclosure to anchor a bottom-up model, a name that ran nearly 3x in nine months on a narrative is more exposed to indiscriminate, valuation-agnostic selling once sentiment turns than a well-covered name would be, and the decline beginning before, not after, a genuinely strong earnings print is consistent with that category of error rather than with a fundamentals-driven reappraisal. RED TEAM AMENDED: this answer is materially weaker than the draft states, on two counts. First, the 'decline began before the print' framing is only half the series. The stock fell 24.34% from the 2026-06-29 peak of 501.13 to 379.17 on 2026-07-24, before the release, and then fell a further 12.72% from 369.00 on 2026-07-27 to 322.06 on 2026-07-29, through the record-revenue, record-backlog print itself. A market selling THROUGH strong results is not obviously making the indiscriminate, valuation-agnostic error this row names; it is at least as consistent with disagreeing about the durability of those results, which is precisely what the base-FCF and margin findings say is the open question. Second, the thin-coverage leg leans on the same analyst_count of 5 that this dive's own crowdedness block rules unusable when it produces an unflattering band. The category of market error is retained as stated but downgraded from a reasoned hypothesis to a contested one, and the verdict rests on it less than the draft implied.
independence_test.falsification: By the Q3 2026 earnings release (expected late October or early November 2026): if backlog growth decelerates back toward MYR Group's own trailing multi-year average pace (high single digits YoY) rather than sustaining the high-teens growth seen in Q2 2026, AND consolidated operating margin falls back under 6.0%, the 'thin-coverage overreaction' reading is wrong and the drawdown correctly anticipated a genuine slowdown in the business, not just in the stock.

earnings_quality.basis: Grade B: a clean mechanical core carrying two mild, disclosed and defensible flags, not a clean A and not a Beneish-breach C. Clean: Beneish M-score of -2.206 against the -1.78 review threshold (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found); Piotroski 8 of 9 (STRONG, 9 of 9 inputs found), the sole miss being a modest current-ratio decline (1.400 FY2024 to 1.334 FY2025) consistent with funding backlog growth through working capital rather than a liquidity problem; Altman Z of 5.97 (SAFE); DSO improved to 60.25 days in FY2025 from a 70.90-day spike in FY2024, no sustained upward drift; capex-to-depreciation stable in a 1.17x to 1.43x band across FY2022-2025, unremarkable for a growing fleet-and-equipment contractor; no auditor change or CFO turnover found (Kelly Huntington has held the CFO role since February 2023 per web search, not exhaustive), no related-party dealings found in the fetched document. Flags: (1) accruals of -13.29% of average assets in FY2025 (net income $118.416M against operating cash flow $326.567M, average total assets $1,566.4415M) exceed even the 10% review-band magnitude the analyst-sources base rates flag for accrual quality, and the swing has been widening (FY2023 +1.34%, FY2024 -3.71%, FY2025 -13.29%); the direction is conservative, cash exceeds earnings rather than the aggressive earnings-inflating direction the accrual-anomaly literature actually warns about, but the magnitude and the trend are large enough to name rather than wave through, and the profile's own risk note calls this level of cash conversion probable working-capital timing rather than durable conversion for a percentage-of-completion contractor; (2) the company's own multi-year earnings record is genuinely volatile at a scale that matters for a $4.6B issuer: FY2024 operating income of $54.082M was less than half FY2023's $129.093M on essentially flat revenue, which the industry's percentage-of-completion accounting attributes to unfavorable cost-estimate revisions on fixed-price contracts, the same mechanism now running favorably in FY2025 and H1 2026 per management's own language ('favorable job close outs'). Not A because of (1) and (2); not C because neither is a Beneish breach, a sustained DSO or deferred-revenue drift, or an undisclosed one-time claim, everything above is on the face of the filing or the companyfacts series. The grade does not cap this dive's verdict: WATCH is reached on the expectations-gap and crowdedness analysis, not on the earnings-quality veto.

challenges.attack: Re-run for Ron's 2026-09-03 would-buy-zone rule (method section 7, WATCH requires a would_buy_zone or a named cap). The zone was drawn by re-basing quality.reverse_dcf's own bisection formula onto the four-year average FCF ($80.020M, replacing the 2.90x-outlier FY2025 base_fcf) and solving forward for the price at which the expectations_gap revenue_cagr_5y row's defended 8.5% growth closes: $113.44 (5y horizon) to $136.48 (10y horizon). Entry-basis stress (stocky.md section 2): does that zone survive the bear case already on this file, that cash conversion does not scale with revenue, or is it the base case with a haircut?
challenges.outcome: LANDED. The zone is not a naive base-case haircut: rebasing off the four-year average already absorbs one negative FCF year (FY2023, -$13.720M) and does not assume the current cash-conversion improvement persists. But it does assume the four-year average conversion rate holds FLAT as revenue grows at the defended 8.5%, and this file's own bear[0] finding is that conversion does not hold flat, it degrades: average revenue rose 63.8% against average free cash flow up only 24.6% between the FY2018-2021 and FY2022-2025 windows, a conversion ratio of 0.386. Applying that ratio to the 8.5% revenue assumption (0.386 x 8.5% = 3.28% FCF growth) and re-solving the identical rebased formula moves fair value to $92.64 (5y) and $94.76 (10y), 18% to 30% below the drawn zone and only just inside the 0.3x last-close floor ($88.33). The drawn zone is therefore optimistic relative to this file's own capture finding: it survives as a stated, arithmetic-backed level under the flat-conversion assumption named in its basis, but a buyer who takes bear[0] at face value has a materially lower true entry point than would_buy_zone states. Recorded here rather than silently redrawn: the zone's derivation method (rebase to the four-year average, solve to the defended growth row) was specified by the mission brief as the honest measure, and this attack's job is to say where that measure is fragile, not to keep re-solving until a number feels safe. would_buy_zone is left as drawn; a buyer applying this file's own capture math should treat $113.44-$136.48 as the upper half of the true range, not its center.

pre_mortem: Wrong by omission, the likeliest of the three. The FY2025 cash conversion turns out to be the new normal rather than a working-capital swing, the margin step-up holds because the work mix genuinely shifted toward interconnect and data-centre scope, the 7.0% bar is cleared without effort, and WATCH at 294.42 was a full round-trip of the 2026 leg handed back for free. The red team's own central finding is the reason this happens: calling the base unmeasurable is symmetric, and an unmeasurable base can surprise upward exactly as easily as downward.

Wrong by generosity. FY2026 free cash flow reverts toward the $80.020M four-year average, the favourable job close-outs roll off and operating margin falls back through the 3.522% eight-year mean, and the stock works down through 288.85 toward the 221.80 lowest-2026 close or the pre-run base. In that world the market was right to sell through the July print, TOO_LATE was the correct call at 294.42, and WATCH was a refusal to make a directional call that the evidence already supported.

Right verdict, dead triggers. WATCH becomes a parking space: the replacement price trigger sits 1.93% away and fires on the next ordinary down week, saying nothing; the PCS trigger cannot resolve because it depends on a positive-control fixture being repaired in a venue this dive does not control; and the review_by date passes with the file re-run mechanically rather than re-decided. The name is never re-examined at a price that mattered, which is the failure mode a WATCH with five triggers is supposed to prevent and the one my own log has no denominator for yet.
red_team.market_would_have_been_right_because: A percentage-of-completion contractor's single best free-cash-flow year, at 2.90x its own four-year average and arriving with a -13.29% accrual reading, is exactly what a working-capital swing looks like from outside. The market sold this name 12.72% across a record-revenue, record-backlog print, which is the behaviour of buyers pricing a conversion reversal rather than of momentum holders leaving indiscriminately. If that is what happened, the drawdown was a repricing and not an overreaction, and the dive's whole reason for interest was an artifact of the base year the reverse DCF happened to stand on.
red_team.surviving_bear_case: MYR Group is a bid-competed electrical contractor whose cash generation does not scale with its revenue, and the one number that made it look cheap is an outlier. Over the eight years on disk, average revenue rose 63.8% between the FY2018-2021 and FY2022-2025 windows while average free cash flow rose only 24.6% and free-cash-flow margin fell from 3.08% to 2.34%, with FCF negative in FY2023; that is the capture ceiling measured from the filings rather than assigned by a chain score. The reverse DCF that produces the cheap-looking 7.0% five-year bar stands on FY2025 free cash flow of $232.195M, which is 2.90x that four-year average and comes from the year the dive itself flags at -13.29% accruals to average assets, so on a normalised base the enterprise value is 55.45x free cash flow rather than 19.11x and the claimed 1.50pp growth gap is both inside the file's own 1.95pp horizon spread and measured across mismatched categories. The margin assumption carrying the bull case, 5.5% steady state, is above every one of the eight fiscal years on record (1.608% to 4.746%, mean 3.522%) and the only mechanism the dive quotes for the current level is management's own non-recurring favourable job close-outs, in a P&L where operating income fell 58.1% on a 7.7% revenue decline two years ago. And the market is not asleep on any of this: the stock gapped 19.85% in a single session in April, ran 2.883x off its 2025 low, and then sold off 41.25%, including 12.72% through a record quarter, so the thin-coverage-overreaction story the dive uses to explain why it is right is contested by the same price series it cites. The bear case is not that the growth is fake, the growth reconstructs exactly from the filings at 16.06% LTM; it is that at this link the growth has never been worth what the multiple is paying for it.
